extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge
extraction.description: A challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering containing 12,247 multiple-choice questions generated from ConceptNet to test models' ability to use prior world knowledge.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.publisher: Tel-Aviv University, Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
extraction.citeAs: Talmor, A., Herzig, J., Lourie, N., & Berant, J. (2019). COMMONSENSE QA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge. arXiv:1811.00937.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by extracting subgraphs from ConceptNet and asking Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) crowd-workers to author multiple-choice questions that discriminate between target concepts. Workers also added distractors and verified question quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet knowledge base (Speer et al., 2017) and web snippets retrieved via Google search.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Triplets from ConceptNet were filtered based on relation type, concept length, and edit distance. Subgraphs were sampled to create question sets. Questions were verified by a disjoint group of workers; 15% of questions were filtered out if not verified by at least one worker answering correctly.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered to ensure quality. Web snippets were retrieved for each question and candidate answer to provide context for reading comprehension models. Data was split into training/development/test sets (80/10/10) using random and question concept splits.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk authored questions and answers. A separate group of workers verified the questions by selecting the correct answer or marking them as unanswerable. Only questions verified by at least one correct worker were included.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A sample of 100 examples was manually annotated with commonsense skills (e.g., Spatial, Cause & Effect) to analyze the types of knowledge required. Annotation artifacts and surface clues were analyzed to understand model performance.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers. 122 formulators contributed, with 10 workers formulating more than 85% of the questions. Verifiers were a disjoint group of workers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to investigate the gap between human and machine commonsense reasoning, highlighting that current NLU systems struggle with background knowledge that is trivial for humans.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may suffer from reporting bias as questions often require background knowledge seldom explicitly reported on the web. There is also a concentration of question formulation by a small number of workers (10 workers formulated >85% of questions).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to English concepts and relations. Performance on web snippets was low, suggesting they do not carry much useful information for this task. The dataset focuses on specific types of commonsense relations and may not cover all aspects of common sense.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of Natural Language Understanding (NLU) models, specifically for commonsense question answering.
